english_draft: Meta reported Q2 2026 results. Revenue was USD 60.801 billion, up 28% year over year. Operating income was USD 18.775 billion, down 8% year over year. Operating margin was 31%, down from 43% a year ago. Diluted EPS was USD 6.18. Costs and expenses were USD 42.026 billion. This amount included USD 2.40 billion of legal charges and USD 1.18 billion of severance from a May 2026 headcount reduction. The May 2026 headcount reduction was a company action. Family daily active people averaged 3.60 billion in June 2026. Ad impressions grew 14% year over year. Average ad price grew 12% year over year. Capital expenditure including finance leases was USD 31.08 billion. The company guided Q3 2026 revenue to USD 61 billion to USD 64 billion. This is a company forecast, not a market consensus. There was no Preview written before the report. A later historical reconstruction draft exists. It cannot be used to verify the original judgment because it was not written before the report.
reader_questions: Why did revenue rise 28% but operating income fall 8%?
Why did operating margin fall from 43% to 31%?
What evidence distinguishes company guidance from market consensus?
